# Overview

Analysis code for the paper *Psychological Determinants of Renewable District
Heating Acceptance: A Theory of Planned Behavior Study*.

Run the document from top to bottom. Every chunk saves its results to
`outputs/` (CSV or RDS), so each number in the paper can be traced to a file.

| Section of this document | Used in the paper |
|---|---|
| Data Preparation, Missing Data | 4.5 Data Analysis (MCAR test), 5.1 Sample Characteristics |
| Scale Construction | 4.3 Questionnaire Development (weighted beliefs), 5.2 (PBC item decision) |
| Descriptive Statistics, Reliability | 5.2–5.3, Table 1, Table 3 |
| Confirmatory Factor Analysis | 5.2, Table 1 (CR, AVE), Table 2 |
| Multicollinearity | 5.2, Table 1 (VIF) |
| Structural Model (main model: place identity via beliefs) | 5.4–5.4.3, Figure 2 |
| Earlier Specification (place identity -> constructs) | 5.4.3 (comparison) |
| Robustness: Demographic Controls | 5.4.4 |

Data note: the questionnaire also contained an item on acceptable price premiums
(`WVT`). It does not measure willingness to pay in an incentive-compatible way
and is therefore **not analyzed**. It remains in the raw data.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 12, fig.height = 8, dpi = 300
)

set.seed(12345)

# All packages are loaded here (installed on first run if missing)
if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(
  haven, dplyr, tidyr, tibble, here,   # data handling
  naniar, MissMech,                    # missing data
  psych, car,                          # reliability, VIF
  lavaan, semTools                     # CFA / SEM
)

for (d in c("data", "outputs")) {
  if (!dir.exists(here(d))) dir.create(here(d))
}
```

# Data Preparation

## Data Import

Public SPSS file; value labels are stripped in the next step. In the public
file, exact age is replaced by 10-year age groups (`Age_group`, see
`code/00_make_public_data.R`).

```{r load_data}
data_raw <- haven::read_spss(
  here("data", "raw", "Survey_Data_public.sav"),
  user_na = FALSE
)

cat("Original sample size:", nrow(data_raw), "\n")
cat("Variables:", ncol(data_raw), "\n")
```

## Data Cleaning

Remove SPSS labels and recode `Gender` and `Zeitung` (newspaper) as factors.

```{r clean_data}
data <- data_raw %>%
  haven::zap_labels() %>%
  haven::zap_formats() %>%
  mutate(
    Gender = factor(Gender, levels = c(1, 2, 3),
                    labels = c("female", "male", "diverse")),
    Zeitung = factor(Zeitung, levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5),
                     labels = c("Neue Westfälische", "Westfalen Blatt",
                                "Die Glocke", "andere", "keine")),
    ID = as.character(ID)
  ) %>%
  select(-any_of("miss_all"))

saveRDS(data, here("data", "01_data_cleaned.rds"))
```

# Missing Data Analysis

Purpose: describe missingness and test whether it is completely at random
(MCAR). The result supports the use of full-information ML in the SEM
(Section 4.5).

## Variable Selection

All variables that enter the analyses.

```{r define_variables}
sem_variables <- c(
  # TPB constructs
  "GB_AtGu", "GB_AtAt", "GB_AtGuen",        # Attitude
  "GB_NormSup", "GB_NormSelf",              # Subjective norm
  "GB_Int1", "GB_Int2", "GB_Int3",          # Intention
  "GB_PBCeasy",                             # PBC (single item)

  # Place identity
  "PlaceID1", "PlaceID2", "PlaceID3",

  # Behavioral beliefs and outcome evaluations
  "BB_Unabh", "BB_PStabil", "BB_Preis", "BB_Klima",
  "BBOE_Unabh", "BBOE_PStabil", "BBOE_Preis", "BBOE_Klima",

  # Control beliefs and control facilitation
  "CB_Preis", "CB_Aufwand", "CB_Förder",
  "CF_Preis", "CF_Aufwand", "CF_Förder",

  # Normative beliefs
  "NB_Fam", "NB_UmM", "NB_Freunde", "NB_Gen",

  # Demographics
  "Age_group", "Gender"
)
```

## Missing Data Pattern

```{r missing_summary}
miss_summary <- naniar::miss_var_summary(data[, sem_variables])

knitr::kable(miss_summary %>% filter(n_miss > 0))

cat("\nTotal observations:", nrow(data), "\n")
cat("Missing cells:", sum(is.na(data[, sem_variables])), "\n")
cat("Percentage missing:",
    round(100 * mean(is.na(data[, sem_variables])), 2), "%\n")
cat("Complete cases:", sum(complete.cases(data[, sem_variables])), "\n")

write.csv(
  data.frame(
    variable = miss_summary$variable,
    n_miss   = as.numeric(miss_summary$n_miss),
    pct_miss = as.numeric(miss_summary$pct_miss)
  ),
  here("outputs", "02_missing_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE
)
```

## Hawkins Test and Non-parametric MCAR Test

Little's MCAR test assumes multivariate normality. The Hawkins test checks this
assumption; if it is rejected, the non-parametric MCAR test of Jamshidian and
Jalal (2010) is used instead (`MissMech`).

```{r hawkins_and_mcar_test}
data_numeric <- data[, sem_variables] |>
  dplyr::select(dplyr::where(is.numeric))

mcar_prelim <- MissMech::TestMCARNormality(data_numeric)

# Labeled output of the package, to verify which p-value is which
summary(mcar_prelim)

hawkins_p <- mcar_prelim$pvalcomb    # Hawkins test (normality / homoscedasticity)
np_p      <- mcar_prelim$pnormality  # p-value reported as non-parametric MCAR test

cat("Hawkins test: p =", format(hawkins_p, scientific = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Non-parametric MCAR test: p =", round(np_p, 4), "\n")

write.csv(
  data.frame(Test = c("Hawkins", "Non-parametric MCAR"),
             p_value = c(hawkins_p, np_p)),
  here("outputs", "03_mcar_tests.csv"), row.names = FALSE
)
```

The Hawkins test rejected multivariate normality (*p* = `r format(hawkins_p, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3)`), so Little's parametric MCAR test would be unreliable. The non-parametric MCAR test did not reject the MCAR hypothesis (*p* = `r round(np_p, 3)`).

# Scale Construction

## Reliability Check for PBC Items

The two PBC items (`GB_PBCeasy` = capacity/ease, `GB_PBC_SD` = autonomy) were
tested for internal consistency. This check was added after the first
reliability analysis and determines how PBC is operationalized.

```{r pbc_reliability_check}
pbc_alpha <- psych::alpha(data %>% select(GB_PBCeasy, GB_PBC_SD))

cat("PBC reliability with 2 items: Cronbach's alpha =",
    round(pbc_alpha$total$raw_alpha, 3), "\n\n")
knitr::kable(pbc_alpha$item.stats[, c("r.cor", "r.drop")])
knitr::kable(pbc_alpha$alpha.drop[, "raw_alpha", drop = FALSE])

if (pbc_alpha$total$raw_alpha < 0.60) {
  cat("\nAlpha < .60: GB_PBC_SD is excluded; PBC = GB_PBCeasy only.\n")
}
```

Due to insufficient internal consistency (α = `r round(pbc_alpha$total$raw_alpha, 2)`), `GB_PBC_SD` was excluded. PBC is operationalized as a single item (`GB_PBCeasy`).

## Create Weighted Belief Variables

Following the expectancy-value logic of the TPB, each belief is multiplied by
its outcome evaluation (behavioral beliefs) or control facilitation (control
beliefs). Normative beliefs (`NB_*`) enter unweighted.

```{r create_weighted_beliefs}
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    # Behavioral beliefs x outcome evaluations
    Gewichtete_BB_Unabh        = BB_Unabh  * BBOE_Unabh,
    Gewichtete_BB_Preisstabili = BB_PStabil * BBOE_PStabil,
    Gewichtete_BB_Preis        = BB_Preis  * BBOE_Preis,
    Gewichtete_BB_Klima        = BB_Klima  * BBOE_Klima,

    # Control beliefs x control facilitation
    Gewichtete_CB_Preis        = CB_Preis    * CF_Preis,
    Gewichtete_CB_Aufwand      = CB_Aufwand  * CF_Aufwand,
    Gewichtete_CB_Foerder      = CB_Förder   * CF_Förder
  )

saveRDS(data, here("data", "04_data_with_beliefs.rds"))
```

## Construct TPB Scales

Scale means are used for descriptives, correlations and VIF. The SEM uses the
latent constructs. `na.rm = FALSE`: a scale score is missing if any item is
missing.

```{r construct_scales}
data <- data %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    Attitude_Scale  = mean(c(GB_AtGu, GB_AtAt, GB_AtGuen), na.rm = FALSE),
    Norm_Scale      = mean(c(GB_NormSup, GB_NormSelf), na.rm = FALSE),
    Intention_Scale = mean(c(GB_Int1, GB_Int2, GB_Int3), na.rm = FALSE),
    PlaceID_Scale   = mean(c(PlaceID1, PlaceID2, PlaceID3), na.rm = FALSE),
    PBC_Scale       = GB_PBCeasy   # single item
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

saveRDS(data, here("data", "05_data_with_scales.rds"))
```

## Derived Variables for the Robustness Check

`female` (1 = female, 0 = male; "diverse" and missing set to NA, because the
group is too small for a separate estimate) and `Age_dec` (midpoint of the
10-year age group in decades, so that the coefficient can be read as the effect
per decade; the open group 75+ is set to 80 years). Used only in the robustness
section.

```{r derived_variables}
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    female  = case_when(Gender == "female" ~ 1,
                        Gender == "male"   ~ 0,
                        TRUE ~ NA_real_),
    Age_dec = c(21, 29.5, 39.5, 49.5, 59.5, 69.5, 80)[Age_group] / 10
  )
```

# Reliability Analysis

Cronbach's alpha and McDonald's omega for the multi-item scales.

```{r reliability_analysis}
scales_list <- list(
  Attitude  = c("GB_AtGu", "GB_AtAt", "GB_AtGuen"),
  Norm      = c("GB_NormSup", "GB_NormSelf"),
  Intention = c("GB_Int1", "GB_Int2", "GB_Int3"),
  PlaceID   = c("PlaceID1", "PlaceID2", "PlaceID3")
)

reliability_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(scales_list), function(s) {
  items <- data[, scales_list[[s]]]
  data.frame(
    Scale   = s,
    N_Items = length(scales_list[[s]]),
    Alpha   = round(psych::alpha(items)$total$raw_alpha, 3),
    Omega   = round(psych::omega(items, nfactors = 1, plot = FALSE)$omega.tot, 3)
  )
}))

knitr::kable(reliability_table)
write.csv(reliability_table, here("outputs", "07_reliability.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Confirmatory Factor Analysis

Measurement model for the four latent constructs. PBC is a single item and
therefore not part of the CFA. Estimator: MLR with FIML for missing values.

```{r cfa_model}
cfa_vars <- c("GB_AtGu", "GB_AtAt", "GB_AtGuen",
              "GB_NormSup", "GB_NormSelf",
              "GB_Int1", "GB_Int2", "GB_Int3",
              "PlaceID1", "PlaceID2", "PlaceID3")

# Cases with no valid answer on any CFA item carry no information
data_cfa <- data %>%
  filter(rowSums(!is.na(select(., all_of(cfa_vars)))) > 0)

cat("Cases removed (all CFA items missing):", nrow(data) - nrow(data_cfa), "\n")
cat("Cases for CFA:", nrow(data_cfa), "\n\n")

cfa_model <- '
  Attitude  =~ GB_AtGu + GB_AtAt + GB_AtGuen
  Norm      =~ GB_NormSup + GB_NormSelf
  Intention =~ GB_Int1 + GB_Int2 + GB_Int3
  PlaceID   =~ PlaceID1 + PlaceID2 + PlaceID3
'

fit_cfa <- cfa(cfa_model, data = data_cfa, missing = "fiml", estimator = "MLR")

summary(fit_cfa, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)
saveRDS(fit_cfa, here("outputs", "08_cfa_model.rds"))
```

## Model Fit Indices

```{r cfa_fit}
fit_indices <- fitMeasures(fit_cfa, c("chisq.scaled", "df.scaled", "pvalue.scaled",
                                      "cfi.robust", "tli.robust",
                                      "rmsea.robust", "rmsea.ci.lower.robust",
                                      "rmsea.ci.upper.robust", "srmr"))

knitr::kable(round(fit_indices, 3))
write.csv(data.frame(Index = names(fit_indices), Value = as.numeric(fit_indices)),
          here("outputs", "08_cfa_fit.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

Standardized loadings with SE, z and p. Unstandardized loadings:
`parameterEstimates(fit_cfa)`.

```{r cfa_loadings}
loadings <- standardizedSolution(fit_cfa) %>%
  filter(op == "=~") %>%
  select(lhs, rhs, est.std, se, z, pvalue) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3)))

knitr::kable(loadings)
write.csv(loadings, here("outputs", "08_factor_loadings.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Composite Reliability and AVE

```{r cfa_cr_ave}
cr_values  <- semTools::compRelSEM(fit_cfa, tau.eq = FALSE, return.total = FALSE)
ave_values <- semTools::AVE(fit_cfa)

cr_ave <- data.frame(
  Construct = names(ave_values),
  CR  = round(cr_values, 3),
  AVE = round(ave_values, 3)
)

knitr::kable(cr_ave)
write.csv(cr_ave, here("outputs", "08_cr_ave.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Discriminant Validity (Fornell-Larcker)

Diagonal = square root of AVE; off-diagonal = latent correlations. Discriminant
validity holds if each diagonal value exceeds the correlations in its row and
column.

```{r fornell_larcker}
fornell_larcker <- lavInspect(fit_cfa, "cor.lv")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(cr_ave))) {
  fornell_larcker[i, i] <- sqrt(cr_ave$AVE[i])
}

knitr::kable(round(fornell_larcker, 3))
write.csv(round(fornell_larcker, 3), here("outputs", "08_fornell_larcker.csv"))
```

# Multicollinearity Check

Variance inflation factors in a regression of intention on the scale scores of
the four predictors (complete cases).

```{r vif_analysis}
vif_data <- data %>%
  select(Attitude_Scale, Norm_Scale, PBC_Scale, PlaceID_Scale, Intention_Scale) %>%
  na.omit()

vif_model  <- lm(Intention_Scale ~ Attitude_Scale + Norm_Scale + PBC_Scale + PlaceID_Scale,
                 data = vif_data)
vif_values <- car::vif(vif_model)

knitr::kable(round(vif_values, 3))
write.csv(data.frame(Predictor = names(vif_values), VIF = round(vif_values, 3)),
          here("outputs", "09_vif.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

All VIF values are below `r round(max(vif_values), 2)`; multicollinearity is not a concern.

# Structural Model (Main Model)

## Model Specification

The main model follows the TPB (Ajzen, 2020): place identity is a background
factor that acts on intention **only through the beliefs**.

    place identity -> 11 beliefs -> attitude / norm / PBC -> intention

- **H1–H3:** intention is predicted by attitude, norm, PBC (paths `b1`–`b3`).
- **H4:** place identity predicts each belief (paths `c1`–`c11`). It has no
  direct path to the constructs or to intention.
- **Beliefs -> constructs:** every belief predicts all three constructs
  (paths `d<k>_<j>`, k = construct, j = belief).
- **Beliefs are endogenous.** Their residual covariances are freed (lavaan does
  not estimate them automatically for endogenous variables). Because no
  observed exogenous predictor is left, lavaan keeps all cases (FIML).
- **Residual correlations** between the three constructs (Ajzen, 2020).
- **Indirect effects:** `ind_<j>_<k> := c<j> * d<k>_<j> * b<k>` (through belief
  j and construct k), `indb_<j>` (belief j, summed over constructs) and
  `total_indirect` (all paths).

One function builds the syntax for all variants used below, so that the models
differ only in the options given.

```{r define_main_model}
beliefs <- c("Gewichtete_BB_Preis", "Gewichtete_BB_Klima",
             "Gewichtete_BB_Preisstabili", "Gewichtete_BB_Unabh",
             "NB_Fam", "NB_UmM", "NB_Freunde", "NB_Gen",
             "Gewichtete_CB_Preis", "Gewichtete_CB_Aufwand", "Gewichtete_CB_Foerder")
constructs <- c("Attitude", "Norm", "PBC_Scale")
j_idx <- seq_along(beliefs)
k_idx <- seq_along(constructs)

# index -> belief name (labels in the model syntax use the index)
label_key <- data.frame(j = j_idx, belief = beliefs)
print(label_key)

# direct = TRUE : adds direct paths place identity -> constructs (a1-a3)
# controls = TRUE: adds age (10-year groups, in decades) and gender (female = 1) as predictors of
#                  intention, constructs, beliefs and place identity
build_model <- function(direct = FALSE, controls = FALSE) {
  syn_c  <- paste0(beliefs, " ~ c", j_idx, "*PlaceID", collapse = "\n")
  syn_d  <- sapply(k_idx, function(k)
    paste0(constructs[k], " ~ ",
           paste0("d", k, "_", j_idx, "*", beliefs, collapse = " + ")))
  syn_rescov <- paste(combn(beliefs, 2, function(x) paste(x[1], "~~", x[2])),
                      collapse = "\n")
  syn_ind    <- unlist(lapply(j_idx, function(j)
    sapply(k_idx, function(k)
      sprintf("ind_%d_%d := c%d * d%d_%d * b%d", j, k, j, k, j, k))))
  syn_indb   <- sapply(j_idx, function(j)
    sprintf("indb_%d := %s", j, paste0("ind_", j, "_", k_idx, collapse = " + ")))
  syn_total  <- paste("total_indirect :=", paste0("indb_", j_idx, collapse = " + "))

  parts <- c(
    "Attitude  =~ GB_AtGu + GB_AtAt + GB_AtGuen",
    "Norm      =~ GB_NormSup + GB_NormSelf",
    "Intention =~ GB_Int1 + GB_Int2 + GB_Int3",
    "PlaceID   =~ PlaceID1 + PlaceID2 + PlaceID3",
    "Intention ~ b1*Attitude + b2*Norm + b3*PBC_Scale",
    syn_c,
    paste(syn_d, collapse = "\n"),
    "Attitude ~~ Norm",
    "Attitude ~~ PBC_Scale",
    "Norm     ~~ PBC_Scale",
    syn_rescov,
    paste(syn_ind, collapse = "\n"),
    paste(syn_indb, collapse = "\n"),
    syn_total
  )
  if (direct) {
    parts <- c(parts, "Attitude  ~ a1*PlaceID", "Norm      ~ a2*PlaceID",
               "PBC_Scale ~ a3*PlaceID")
  }
  if (controls) {
    parts <- c(parts,
               paste0(c("Intention", constructs, "PlaceID", beliefs),
                      " ~ Age_dec + female", collapse = "\n"))
  }
  paste(parts, collapse = "\n")
}

model_main        <- build_model()
model_main_direct <- build_model(direct = TRUE)
```

## Model Estimation

MLR with FIML (`missing = "ml"`).

```{r estimate_main_model}
fit_main        <- sem(model_main,        data = data, missing = "ml", estimator = "MLR")
fit_main_direct <- sem(model_main_direct, data = data, missing = "ml", estimator = "MLR")
saveRDS(fit_main,        here("outputs", "10_sem_main.rds"))
saveRDS(fit_main_direct, here("outputs", "10_sem_main_direct.rds"))

cat("Cases in sample:", nrow(data), "\n")
cat("Cases used in the SEM:", lavInspect(fit_main, "nobs"), "\n")
```

## Model Fit

```{r main_fit}
fit_idx <- c("chisq.scaled", "df.scaled", "pvalue.scaled",
             "cfi.robust", "tli.robust", "rmsea.robust",
             "rmsea.ci.lower.robust", "rmsea.ci.upper.robust", "srmr")

fit_main_indices <- fitMeasures(fit_main, fit_idx)
knitr::kable(round(fit_main_indices, 3))
write.csv(data.frame(Index = names(fit_main_indices), Value = as.numeric(fit_main_indices)),
          here("outputs", "10_main_fit.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

### Is the belief route sufficient?

Comparison with the model that adds direct paths from place identity to the
three constructs (`fit_main_direct`). A non-significant scaled chi-square
difference means the direct paths are not needed.

```{r main_direct_test}
lavTestLRT(fit_main, fit_main_direct)
```

## Path Coefficients (Section 5.4.1–5.4.3, Figure 2)

Standardized coefficients of all structural paths.

```{r main_paths}
sig_stars <- function(p) case_when(p < 0.001 ~ "***", p < 0.01 ~ "**", p < 0.05 ~ "*", TRUE ~ "")

main_paths <- standardizedSolution(fit_main) %>%
  filter(op == "~") %>%
  select(lhs, rhs, est.std, se, z, pvalue, ci.lower, ci.upper) %>%
  mutate(sig = sig_stars(pvalue), across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3)))

write.csv(main_paths, here("outputs", "11_main_path_coefficients.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

### Core TPB paths (H1–H3)

```{r main_paths_core}
knitr::kable(main_paths %>% filter(lhs == "Intention") %>%
               select(lhs, rhs, est.std, se, pvalue, sig))
```

### Place identity -> beliefs (H4, paths c1–c11)

```{r main_paths_placeid}
knitr::kable(main_paths %>% filter(rhs == "PlaceID", lhs %in% beliefs) %>%
               select(belief = lhs, est.std, se, pvalue, sig) %>%
               arrange(desc(est.std)))
```

### Beliefs -> constructs (exploratory)

```{r main_paths_beliefs}
belief_paths <- main_paths %>% filter(lhs %in% constructs, rhs %in% beliefs) %>%
  arrange(lhs, rhs)

knitr::kable(belief_paths %>% select(lhs, rhs, est.std, se, pvalue, sig))
write.csv(belief_paths, here("outputs", "11_main_belief_paths.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Explained Variance (Figure 2)

R² of intention, the three constructs and the beliefs.

```{r main_r2}
r2_main <- lavInspect(fit_main, "rsquare")[c("Intention", constructs, beliefs)]
r2_table <- data.frame(Variable = names(r2_main), R2 = round(r2_main, 3))

knitr::kable(r2_table, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(r2_table, here("outputs", "11_main_r_squared.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Indirect Effects of Place Identity (H4, Section 5.4.3)

Total indirect effect and the indirect effect per belief (summed over the three
constructs). Two sets of results:

1. Delta method (from the main fit, robust standard errors).
2. Percentile bootstrap, 1000 draws. A product of coefficients is not normally
   distributed, so the bootstrap interval is the primary criterion: an indirect
   effect is supported if its 95% interval does not include zero. Estimator
   `ML` is required for bootstrap standard errors in lavaan; MLR has the same
   point estimates. Runtime: several minutes.

```{r main_indirect}
indirect_delta <- parameterEstimates(fit_main, standardized = TRUE) %>%
  filter(op == ":=", grepl("^(indb_|total_indirect)", label)) %>%
  select(label, est, std.all, se, pvalue)

set.seed(12345)
fit_main_boot <- sem(model_main, data = data, missing = "ml", estimator = "ML",
                     se = "bootstrap", bootstrap = 1000)
saveRDS(fit_main_boot, here("outputs", "11_sem_main_bootstrap.rds"))
cat("Successful bootstrap draws:", nrow(lavInspect(fit_main_boot, "boot")), "of 1000\n")

indirect_boot <- parameterEstimates(fit_main_boot, boot.ci.type = "perc") %>%
  filter(op == ":=", grepl("^(indb_|total_indirect)", label)) %>%
  select(label, ci.lower, ci.upper)

indirect_main <- indirect_delta %>%
  left_join(indirect_boot, by = "label") %>%
  mutate(j = suppressWarnings(as.integer(sub("indb_", "", label)))) %>%
  left_join(label_key, by = "j") %>%
  mutate(effect = ifelse(is.na(belief), "TOTAL", belief),
         zero_excluded = ci.lower > 0 | ci.upper < 0,
         across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3))) %>%
  select(effect, est, std.all, se, pvalue, ci.lower, ci.upper, zero_excluded)

knitr::kable(indirect_main,
             caption = "Indirect effects of place identity on intention via beliefs (est = unstandardized)")
write.csv(indirect_main, here("outputs", "11_main_indirect_effects.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Earlier Specification: Place Identity Predicts the Constructs

Earlier specification (reported in the paper for comparison). Place identity
predicts attitude, norm and PBC directly; the 11 beliefs enter as separate
exogenous predictors. This simplifies the TPB: the belief level is not part of
the place identity pathway. Because the beliefs are observed exogenous
predictors (`fixed.x = TRUE`), lavaan drops cases with a missing belief score,
which is why N is smaller than in the main model.

```{r alt_model}
belief_rhs <- paste(beliefs, collapse = " + ")

model_alt <- paste0('
  Attitude  =~ GB_AtGu + GB_AtAt + GB_AtGuen
  Norm      =~ GB_NormSup + GB_NormSelf
  Intention =~ GB_Int1 + GB_Int2 + GB_Int3
  PlaceID   =~ PlaceID1 + PlaceID2 + PlaceID3

  Intention ~ b1*Attitude + b2*Norm + b3*PBC_Scale

  Attitude  ~ a1*PlaceID
  Norm      ~ a2*PlaceID
  PBC_Scale ~ a3*PlaceID

  Attitude  ~ ', belief_rhs, '
  Norm      ~ ', belief_rhs, '
  PBC_Scale ~ ', belief_rhs, '

  Attitude ~~ Norm
  Attitude ~~ PBC_Scale
  Norm     ~~ PBC_Scale

  ind_att        := a1 * b1
  ind_norm       := a2 * b2
  ind_pbc        := a3 * b3
  total_indirect := ind_att + ind_norm + ind_pbc
')

fit_alt <- sem(model_alt, data = data, missing = "ml", estimator = "MLR")
saveRDS(fit_alt, here("outputs", "12_sem_alt.rds"))

cat("Cases with a missing belief score:", sum(!complete.cases(data[, beliefs])), "\n")
cat("Cases used in the SEM:", lavInspect(fit_alt, "nobs"), "\n")

alt_fit <- fitMeasures(fit_alt, fit_idx)
knitr::kable(round(alt_fit, 3))
write.csv(data.frame(Index = names(alt_fit), Value = as.numeric(alt_fit)),
          here("outputs", "12_alt_fit.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Paths, R² and Indirect Effects

```{r alt_results}
alt_paths <- standardizedSolution(fit_alt) %>%
  filter(op == "~", lhs == "Intention" | rhs == "PlaceID") %>%
  select(lhs, rhs, est.std, se, pvalue) %>%
  mutate(sig = sig_stars(pvalue), across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3)))
knitr::kable(alt_paths)

cat("R² intention:", round(lavInspect(fit_alt, "rsquare")["Intention"], 3), "\n")

# Delta method
alt_indirect <- parameterEstimates(fit_alt, standardized = TRUE) %>%
  filter(op == ":=") %>%
  select(label, est, std.all, se, pvalue) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3)))
knitr::kable(alt_indirect, caption = "Earlier specification: indirect effects (delta method)")

# Percentile bootstrap (estimator ML, see above)
set.seed(12345)
fit_alt_boot <- sem(model_alt, data = data, missing = "ml", estimator = "ML",
                    se = "bootstrap", bootstrap = 1000)
alt_boot <- parameterEstimates(fit_alt_boot, boot.ci.type = "perc") %>%
  filter(op == ":=") %>%
  select(label, est, ci.lower, ci.upper) %>%
  mutate(zero_excluded = ci.lower > 0 | ci.upper < 0,
         across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3)))
knitr::kable(alt_boot, caption = "Earlier specification: indirect effects (bootstrap)")

write.csv(alt_paths,    here("outputs", "12_alt_paths.csv"),          row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(alt_indirect, here("outputs", "12_alt_indirect_delta.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(alt_boot,     here("outputs", "12_alt_indirect_boot.csv"),  row.names = FALSE)
```

## Why does the fit differ? (diagnostic)

The earlier specification fits worse than the main model. A possible
reason is that it does not model the relation between place identity and the
beliefs. The residual correlations between the place identity items and the
beliefs show whether this is the case (large absolute values = unexplained
association).

```{r alt_residuals}
rc <- tryCatch(residuals(fit_alt, type = "cor")$cov, error = function(e) NULL)
pid_items <- c("PlaceID1", "PlaceID2", "PlaceID3")
if (!is.null(rc) && all(beliefs %in% colnames(rc))) {
  knitr::kable(round(rc[pid_items, beliefs], 2))
} else {
  cat("Residual correlations for the beliefs are not available in this fit.\n")
}
```

# Robustness Check: Demographic Controls (Section 5.4.4)

Demographic effects were not part of the original analysis. This section tests
whether age and gender change the results of the main model.

- **Controls:** age (10-year groups, coded in decades) and gender (female = 1) predict intention, the
  three constructs, place identity and all beliefs (`model_demo`).
- **Sample:** respondents with valid age and binary gender only (`data_robust`;
  "diverse" is excluded because the group is too small for a separate estimate).
- **Reference:** the main model estimated on the same sample (`fit_base`), so
  that differences are due to the controls and not to the changed sample.

## Sample

```{r robustness_data}
data_robust <- data %>% filter(!is.na(female), !is.na(Age_dec))

cat("Full sample:", nrow(data), "\n")
cat("Excluded (diverse or missing gender/age):", nrow(data) - nrow(data_robust), "\n")
cat("Robustness sample:", nrow(data_robust), "\n")
```

## Models and Estimation

```{r robustness_models}
model_demo <- build_model(controls = TRUE)

fit_base <- sem(model_main, data = data_robust, missing = "ml", estimator = "MLR")
fit_demo <- sem(model_demo, data = data_robust, missing = "ml", estimator = "MLR")
saveRDS(fit_base, here("outputs", "13_sem_base.rds"))
saveRDS(fit_demo, here("outputs", "13_sem_demo.rds"))

nobs_table <- data.frame(
  Model  = c("Main model (full sample)", "Reference (robustness sample)",
             "With demographic controls"),
  N_used = c(lavInspect(fit_main, "nobs"), lavInspect(fit_base, "nobs"),
             lavInspect(fit_demo, "nobs"))
)
knitr::kable(nobs_table)
write.csv(nobs_table, here("outputs", "13_robustness_nobs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Comparison of Path Coefficients

```{r robustness_paths}
get_paths <- function(fit, suffix) {
  standardizedSolution(fit) %>%
    filter(op == "~", !(rhs %in% c("Age_dec", "female"))) %>%
    select(lhs, rhs, est.std, pvalue) %>%
    rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_", suffix), c(est.std, pvalue))
}

path_comparison <- get_paths(fit_base, "base") %>%
  full_join(get_paths(fit_demo, "demo"), by = c("lhs", "rhs")) %>%
  mutate(diff_demo_base = est.std_demo - est.std_base,
         sig_change     = (pvalue_base < .05) != (pvalue_demo < .05)) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3))) %>%
  arrange(lhs, rhs)

knitr::kable(path_comparison,
             caption = "Standardized paths without vs. with demographic controls")

cat("\nLargest absolute change from controls:",
    max(abs(path_comparison$diff_demo_base), na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Paths changing significance (p < .05):",
    sum(path_comparison$sig_change, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

if (any(path_comparison$sig_change, na.rm = TRUE)) {
  knitr::kable(path_comparison %>% filter(sig_change) %>%
                 select(lhs, rhs, est.std_base, pvalue_base, est.std_demo, pvalue_demo),
               caption = "Paths whose significance changes")
}

write.csv(path_comparison, here("outputs", "13_robustness_path_comparison.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Demographic Effects

`std.all` for age (continuous); `std.nox` for gender (binary, so the predictor
is left unstandardized).

```{r robustness_demo_effects}
demo_effects <- parameterEstimates(fit_demo, standardized = TRUE) %>%
  filter(op == "~", rhs %in% c("Age_dec", "female")) %>%
  select(lhs, rhs, est, se, pvalue, std.all, std.nox) %>%
  mutate(sig = sig_stars(pvalue), across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3))) %>%
  arrange(rhs, lhs)

knitr::kable(demo_effects, caption = "Effects of age (per decade) and gender (female = 1)")
write.csv(demo_effects, here("outputs", "13_robustness_demo_effects.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Indirect Effects, R² and Model Fit

Bootstrap intervals (1000 draws, estimator `ML`) for the total indirect effect
with and without controls. Runtime: several minutes.

```{r robustness_summary}
boot_total <- function(model, d) {
  set.seed(12345)
  f <- sem(model, data = d, missing = "ml", estimator = "ML",
           se = "bootstrap", bootstrap = 1000)
  parameterEstimates(f, boot.ci.type = "perc") %>%
    filter(op == ":=", label == "total_indirect") %>%
    select(est, ci.lower, ci.upper)
}

indirect_comparison <- bind_rows(
  boot_total(model_main, data_robust) %>% mutate(Model = "Reference (robustness sample)"),
  boot_total(model_demo, data_robust) %>% mutate(Model = "With demographic controls")
) %>%
  mutate(zero_excluded = ci.lower > 0 | ci.upper < 0,
         across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3)))

knitr::kable(indirect_comparison, caption = "Total indirect effect of place identity (bootstrap)")
write.csv(indirect_comparison, here("outputs", "13_robustness_indirect.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

fits <- list(fit_main, fit_base, fit_demo)
summary_table <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Main model (full sample)", "Reference (robustness sample)",
            "With demographic controls"),
  N = sapply(fits, lavInspect, what = "nobs"),
  R2_Intention = unname(sapply(fits, function(f) lavInspect(f, "rsquare")["Intention"])),
  do.call(rbind, lapply(fits, fitMeasures, fit.measures = fit_idx[c(1:6, 9)]))
) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3)))

knitr::kable(summary_table, caption = "Sample size, R² of intention and model fit")
write.csv(summary_table, here("outputs", "13_robustness_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```
